statement: Let U(N)=1-F(N). If dF/dN=h(N)(1-F), then dU/dN=-h(N)U and U(N)=exp[-integral_0^N h(s)ds].
If activation thresholds form a Poisson process over expansion-load measure dmu=h(N)dN, then F(N)=P(N_th<N)=1-exp[-mu([0,N])].
If h(N)=(nu/u_s)(N/u_s)^(nu-1), then mu([0,N])=(N/u_s)^nu and F(N)=1-exp[-(N/u_s)^nu].
The parent action/corpus still does not derive why the activation measure density must scale as N^(nu-1), nor why nu equals 7/4.
The equality clock gives a natural scale u_eq, but the parent theory does not derive alpha_act or an exact F(u_eq) rule.
